goal: Apply exact selected, invalid, snap-guide and legacy-conflict visuals with zoom compensation while preserving transient-state and warm-white compatibility rules.
non_goals: Do not change collision acceptance, geometry-session, relation, AI, chat, persistence, credential, packaging or release behavior.
Do not persist selection, invalid, snap-guide or legacy-conflict visual state in CanvasNodeData, history or SQLite.
Do not add or upgrade dependencies.
Do not read, print or modify provider credentials.
acceptance_criteria: Visual contracts assert the exact approved selection, invalid, legacy-conflict, text background, text color and border colors.

Selection renders a one-pixel cold-white inner stroke, two-pixel cyan outer stroke and twelve-pixel thirty-two-percent cyan glow with stable screen-space appearance from ten to six-hundred percent zoom.
Invalid red overrides normal preview; legacy conflict keeps an amber dashed inner stroke while selected nodes also retain the cyan outer glow.
Right-click, left-click, right-drag marquee and programmatic evidence focus derive the same selected visual, and an open context menu keeps selection visible.
Snap guides render only in a viewport overlay/portal and are never serialized.
New text blocks persist the warm-white defaults while legacy missing-background blocks render the fallback without rewriting documents; transparency and custom colors win.
Focused visual contract, complete Canvas suite, TypeScript/production build and diff checks pass.
The implementation is committed and independently reviewed.
notes: Read the Task 6 brief first and follow strict TDD.
Preserve the Task 5 collision/session behavior and use its transient visual-state channels.
Keep glow and stroke thickness stable in screen pixels across the approved zoom range.
Use fixed UTF-8 I/O for every non-ASCII read, search, edit and test output.
Do not expose or change configured provider secrets.
